newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil surprised by trade deficit, blames petrol.
newsitem.headline: Brazil surprised by trade deficit, blames petrol.

text.p: The Brazilian government was "surprised" by the size of September's $655 million trade deficit, but noted an unexpected surge in oil imports was largely to blame, said a senior Finance Ministry official.

Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, economic policy secretary, told reporters that without high oil purchases by state oil firm Petrobras the deficit would have been closer to market expectations of $400 million.
Mendonca de Barros said it was difficult to predict the trade balance performance for the rest of the year because September's result had been affected by three unusual variables.
The first was fuel and lubricant imports, which climbed 50.8 percent over August and 58 percent over September 1995.
Mendonca de Barros said he believed Petrobras was stocking up ahead of a possible strike by oil workers and because of improved economic activity.
The second factor was economic recovery.

The official said gross domestic product grew 7.7 percent in the third quarter versus the same period in 1995. He said market forecasts saw 4.0 percent GDP growth in the fourth quarter and year-end growth of 3.0 percent.
The third factor affecting September trade was the lagged effect of a bill removing tax on primary and intermediate exports, which took effect in the middle of the month.
But Mendonca de Barros said the impact was disappointing. "The expected effect was not sustained," he said.
